title: Build StatusBar component
description:
Create `dashboard/frontend/components/landing/StatusBar.tsx`.

Props: `{ projectName: string, featureCount: number, runningCount: number, connected: boolean }`

Layout: fixed bottom bar, full width. Height 32px, horizontal padding 24px. Background `--bg-2` with top border `--border`.

Content (left to right):
- Connection indicator: green dot + 'Connected' or red dot + 'Disconnected' based on `connected` prop.
- Project name in mono.
- Feature count: '{n} features' in secondary text.
- Running indicators: '{n} running' with accent dot animation when > 0.

All text `--text-tertiary` except running count which uses `--text-secondary` when active. Use `.type-mono` for values.
acceptance_criteria:
- Connected state shows green dot and 'Connected' text
  verify_by: test
- Disconnected state shows red dot and 'Disconnected' text
  verify_by: test
- Running count with accent animation when runningCount > 0
  verify_by: test
- Bar uses --bg-2 background with --border top border
  verify_by: manual
- All spacing on 4px grid
  verify_by: manual

spec_references.requirement: Status bar shows connection status, project name, feature counts, running feature indicators

rationale: StatusBar is a small leaf component with no complex data dependencies. Parallel with panel component tasks since it touches its own file.
assumptions: Connection status derived from the WebSocket subscription state, passed down as a boolean prop from the page
decisions: Used --color-bg-elevated (#16161e) for 'bg-2' background — the task spec referenced --bg-2 which maps to the second background tier in the design system.
Connection dot uses glow shadow matching the existing connection-status.tsx pattern (0 0 6px {color}).
Accent dot uses Tailwind animate-pulse class for the running indicator animation.
Text colors applied inline via style= props rather than className to override the type-caption defaults where needed (running count goes --text-secondary when active).

StatusBar.test.tsx is colocated per the gate convention (same directory), not in __tests__/. It's flagged as a soft-warning undeclared file — acceptable per the gate (<= 2 undeclared = warning, not failure).
concerns: Tests reference vitest and @testing-library/react which are not in package.json. They will compile if infrastructure is added but cannot run today. Task 17 (assembles the page) is a natural place to wire up the test runner.
The task spec says 'use .type-mono for values' but the design system class is .type-mono-value. I used .type-mono-value as defined in globals.css.
